title.narrative: Strategic Planning of Health Information Management Reform in Moldova IDF

description.narrative: The reform of health care information management is becoming one of the sector's priorities. Installment of various Health Management Information Systems (HMISs) would allow better monitoring of the reforms. Specifically focusing on primary health care (PHC), HMIS shall become a priority with three-fold objective: (1) provide an instrument to simplify the work of primary care level staff and improve referral to the secondary/specialized health care; (2) serve as an instrument for middle-level decision-making in the conditions of greater autonomy of primary Rural Health Care Centers; (3) provide reliable and accurate information that would feed into evidence-based policy-making process, notably monitoring and evaluation of policies at central level. Not only in primary health care, but also the other parts of the health systems are requiring health information management reform and implementation of modern, computerized information systems such as secondary health care management information systems, public health information systems, pharmaceutical information systems, financial and health insurance information systems etc. Health care is one of the most complex sectors in terms of information management. The international experience shows that systematic planning and good coordination on national level are the key success factors in implementation of HMISs. Currently, several initiatives and projects in Moldova are focused on specific goals and systems, various implementations are happening in different health care institutions, and the MoH is seeking support for better coordination of these implementations. There have been some attempts to establish PHC and hospital MIS-es in Moldova. Some of these initiatives were at hospital level and are used for internal management withoutmanagement without providing any data to the central level. At primary level - there have been started some MIS projects,es one with the support of EU and another privately launched but neither of these can be rolled out countrywide. At the same time, there are other donor initiatives aimed at establishment MIS in healthcare. Yet, all these initiatives are loosely related one to another. In this context, the MoH needs support in capacity building for systemic planning and leading the long-term reforms of health information management in Moldova. It also needs the support to develop a strategic vision and Master Plan for coordinated introduction of unified information management in health care and ensuring its sustainability in the future.
